we developed two types of mAbs against IL-18, which are suitable for Western blot, WES, immunopreciptation and immunofluorescent assays, as well as for function-blocking assays, and that WES analysis of IL-18 in sera of patients with inflammatory diseases showed the cleaved, active IL-18 in some cases.

we have generated and characterized two types of monocloncal antibody against IL-18: anti-IL18 63-68 mAb which recognize full-length IL-181-193 and cleavage product IL-18 37-193; and anti- IL18 neoepitopic mAb which recognize new N-terminal 3YFGKLES 3K4 of IL-18.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the production and application of two types of monoclonals against human interleukin (hIL-18) that recognize full-length IL-1863-193 and the neoepitoep 37YFGKL of cleaved IL-1837.
the generation and characterization of anti-IL-1836-68 and anti-IL18 neoepitopes antibodies with high affinity.
the development of a novel class of mAbs against IL-18 and its cleavage product that will be useful in the diagnosis and therapy of inflammatory diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anti-IL-1837-68 and anti-IL18 neoepitopes mAbs are suitable for the detection of active, mature IL-18 and for the detection of IL-18 in the serum of inflammatory diseases.
the anti-IL-1837-68 mAb and the anti-IL18 neoepitopes mAbs are very useful tools for IL-18 and IL-18-related inflammasomes research.
the anti-IL-18163-68 and anti-IL18 neoepitopes antibodies are useful tools for the detection of IL-18 and for studying the inflammasomes in various inflammatory diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a novel method for the detection of the IL-1837YFGKLESKN44 neoepitope, a novel epitope that is generated by pro-inflammatory caspaes-1/4 in inflammasome-activated IL-18.
we have generated and characterized anti-human IL-18 mAbs with high affinity and two types of anti-IL-1837-68 and anti-neoepitope mAbs.
we generated anti-IL-1 and anti-IL18 monoclonal antibody that can be useful for the diagnosis and therapy of inflammatory diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the development of mAbs against IL-18 and its active form, and the application of the WES method, will provide new tools for the study of IL-18 biology and for the diagnosis and treatment of inflammatory diseases.
we generated two types of monoclonals antibodies that are suitable for various immunoassays and that will be very useful for the study of IL-18 and inflammatory caspases.
